records.source: Τότε ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνήχθη εἰς τὴν ἔρημον ὑπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος, πειρασθῆναι ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου.
records.gloss: Then the Jesus was led up into the wilderness by the Spirit to be tempted by the devil.
pieces: Then the Spirit led Jesus up into the wilderness, where the devil would tempt {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.1: Then Jesus was led up into the wilderness by the Spirit to be tempted by the devil.

R.1: Then the Spirit led Jesus into the desert so that the devil could try to make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} do wrong.

decisions.choice: tempted: put to the test, here by one who wants him to fail
alternatives: tested, as God tests to prove faithfulness
decisions.reason: The verb covers both testing and tempting. God tested Israel in the wilderness (Deuteronomy 8:2); here the devil tries to lead God's Son away from obedience. The Spirit leads him there, so the trial is within God's purpose.

decisions.choice: the wilderness: where Israel was tested for forty years
decisions.reason: Jesus answers each temptation from Deuteronomy 6-8, where Moses recalls Israel's testing in the wilderness. Where Israel failed, God's Son stays faithful.

decisions.choice: the devil: the slanderer, the enemy of God, also called Satan
alternatives: an evil force with no person behind it
decisions.reason: The Greek word means slanderer or accuser. Matthew also calls him "the tempter" (4:3) and Jesus calls him "Satan" (4:10).

decisions.choice: try to make him do wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says what tempting is.

records.heading: The testing of Jesus

records.source: καὶ νηστεύσας ἡμέρας τεσσεράκοντα καὶ νύκτας τεσσεράκοντα ὕστερον ἐπείνασεν.
records.gloss: And having fasted days forty and nights forty, afterward he was hungry.
pieces: He fasted forty days and forty nights, and at the end of it {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was famished.

L.2: And having fasted forty days and forty nights, afterward {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was hungry.

R.2: He went without food for forty days and forty nights. After that, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was very hungry.

decisions.choice: forty days and forty nights: as Moses on the mountain
alternatives: a round number with no echo
decisions.reason: Moses fasted forty days and forty nights before receiving the law (Exodus 34:28; Deuteronomy 9:9), and Elijah traveled forty days and nights to Horeb (1 Kings 19:8). The forty also recalls Israel's forty years in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: afterward he was hungry: weakness that the tempter uses
decisions.reason: The plain words set up the first temptation, which is about bread.

decisions.choice: went without food
decisions.reason: Readable says what fasting is.

records.source: καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ πειράζων εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, εἰπὲ ἵνα οἱ λίθοι οὗτοι ἄρτοι γένωνται.
records.gloss: And having come the tempting [one] said to him, If son you are of the God, say that the stones these loaves become.
pieces: Then the tempter approached {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the Son of God," he said, "command these stones to become loaves of bread."

L.3: And the tempter came and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are [the] Son of God, say that these stones should become loaves of bread."

R.3: The devil came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the Son of God, tell these stones to turn into bread."

decisions.choice: if you are the Son of God: taking up what God has just said (3:17)
alternatives: doubting that he is the Son
decisions.reason: The form of the condition takes the statement as true for the argument. The tempter does not deny that Jesus is the Son; he urges him to use that place for himself.

decisions.choice: stones ... loaves: the round stones of the wilderness looked like small loaves
decisions.reason: Bread was baked in flat, round loaves. The stones of the Judean wilderness have the same size and shape.

decisions.choice: the devil
decisions.reason: Readable names the tempter as the devil of 4:1.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Γέγραπται· Οὐκ ἐπ’ ἄρτῳ μόνῳ ζήσεται ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ παντὶ ῥήματι ἐκπορευομένῳ διὰ στόματος θεοῦ.
records.gloss: He then answering said, It has been written: Not on bread alone will live the man, but on every word coming out through mouth of God.
pieces: But Jesus answered, "Scripture says, 'No one lives on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.'"

L.4: But answering, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "It is written, '{{gender:A person|Man}} will not live on bread alone, but on every word coming out through [the] mouth of God.'"

R.4: But Jesus answered, "The Scriptures say, 'People need more than bread to live. They need every word that God speaks.'"

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 8:3: God fed Israel with manna to teach dependence on his word
alternatives: a general saying about spiritual food
decisions.reason: Moses reminds Israel that God let them go hungry and then fed them manna, to teach them that life comes from what God says. Jesus will not make his own bread; he trusts God to provide.

decisions.choice: it is written: it stands written and has authority
decisions.reason: The perfect tense speaks of Scripture as a word that still stands. Jesus answers each temptation with it.

decisions.choice: the man: a human being, anyone
decisions.reason: The word means a human being in general.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: The tempter has just spoken, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:A person|Man}} (L); No one (B); People (R)
decisions.reason: Literal follows the singular with the gender setting. Balanced and Readable use words that already include everyone.

records.source: Τότε παραλαμβάνει αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν πόλιν, καὶ ἔστησεν αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ πτερύγιον τοῦ ἱεροῦ, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, βάλε σεαυτὸν κάτω· γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ ἐντελεῖται περὶ σοῦ καὶ ἐπὶ χειρῶν ἀροῦσίν σε, μήποτε προσκόψῃς πρὸς λίθον τὸν πόδα σου.
records.gloss: Then takes him the devil into the holy city, and set him on the pinnacle of the temple, \v 6 and says to him, If son you are of the God, throw yourself down; it has been written for that To the angels of him he will command concerning you and on hands they will lift you, lest you strike against a stone the foot of you.
pieces: Then the devil brought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the holy city and set {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the high corner of the temple.

"If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the Son of God," he told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "jump down. For Scripture says, 'He will put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels in charge of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}},' and, 'They will catch {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in their hands, so that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will not strike {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} foot against a stone.'"

L.5: Then the devil takes {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} into the holy city and set {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the pinnacle of the temple,
L.6: and says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are [the] Son of God, throw {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} down, for it is written, 'He will command {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels concerning {{deity_pronoun:you|You}},' and 'On [their] hands they will lift {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} up, so that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not strike {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} foot against a stone.'"

R.5: Then the devil took Jesus to Jerusalem, the holy city. He put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the highest part of the temple.
R.6: He said, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the Son of God, jump off! The Scriptures say, 'God will tell {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels to take care of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. They will catch {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with their hands so that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will not hurt {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} foot on a rock.'"

decisions.choice: the holy city: Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Jerusalem is called the holy city because God's temple stood there (Isaiah 52:1; Matthew 27:53).

decisions.choice: the pinnacle: a high edge of the temple buildings
alternatives: the top of the sanctuary itself
decisions.reason: The word means "little wing", a projecting edge or corner. It may be the corner of the temple courts above the Kidron valley, a drop of well over a hundred feet. The exact place is not known.

decisions.choice: Psalm 91:11-12, quoted by the devil to make God prove his care
decisions.reason: The psalm promises God's protection to one who trusts him. The devil uses it to urge a test of that promise, and leaves out the psalm's "to guard you in all your ways". Jesus answers with another Scripture (4:7).

decisions.choice: takes, says (L); took, told, said (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration; Balanced and Readable use the past.

decisions.choice: jump down (B); jump off (R)
decisions.reason: Everyday words for the same act.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem, the holy city; God will tell his angels
alternatives: the holy city; he will command his angels
decisions.reason: Readable names the city and the speaker of the psalm.

records.source: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πάλιν γέγραπται· Οὐκ ἐκπειράσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου.
records.gloss: Said to him the Jesus, Again it has been written: Not you will test Lord the God of you.
pieces: Jesus answered him, "Scripture says something else as well: 'You must not test the Lord your God.'"

L.7: Jesus said to him, "Again it is written, 'You shall not put [the] Lord your God to the test.'"

R.7: Jesus answered, "The Scriptures also say, 'Do not put the Lord your God to the test.'"

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 6:16: as Israel tested God at Massah
decisions.reason: At Massah the people demanded water and asked, "Is the Lord among us or not?" (Exodus 17:7). To force God to act to prove his care is to test him. Jesus will not make God rescue him to show that he is the Son.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God, whose name stands in the Hebrew
decisions.reason: In Deuteronomy 6:16 the Hebrew has God's name, which the Greek Old Testament gives as "Lord". The Lord your God is the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: again it is written: Scripture set against a misuse of Scripture
alternatives: the same Scripture a second time
decisions.reason: "Again" means "on the other hand": Scripture is read in the light of Scripture.

records.source: Πάλιν παραλαμβάνει αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν λίαν, καὶ δείκνυσιν αὐτῷ πάσας τὰς βασιλείας τοῦ κόσμου καὶ τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ταῦτά σοι πάντα δώσω, ἐὰν πεσὼν προσκυνήσῃς μοι.
records.gloss: Again takes him the devil to a mountain high exceedingly, and shows him all the kingdoms of the world and the glory of them, \v 9 and said to him, These to you all I will give, if falling down you worship me.
pieces: Then the devil led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up a very high mountain and showed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} every kingdom of the world in all its glory.
"I will give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all of this," he told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} kneel down and worship me."

L.8: Again the devil takes {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a very high mountain and shows {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all the kingdoms of the world and their glory,
L.9: and he said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "All these things I will give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} fall down and worship me."

R.8: Next the devil took Jesus to the top of a very high mountain. He showed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all the kingdoms of the world and all their glory.
R.9: The devil said, "I will give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all these things if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will bow down and worship me."

decisions.choice: their glory: their splendor, wealth and power
decisions.reason: Here glory is the outward greatness of earthly kingdoms.

decisions.choice: the offer: rule over the world without the way of obedience
alternatives: an offer the devil had no power to make
decisions.reason: God promised the nations to his Son (Psalm 2:8), and the risen Jesus receives all authority (28:18). The devil offers the same rule at the price of worshiping him. Matthew does not say whether the devil could give it.

decisions.choice: fall down and worship: bow to the ground as to God
decisions.reason: Here the bow is worship in the full sense, as Jesus's answer shows (4:10).

decisions.choice: a very high mountain: perhaps an echo of Moses viewing the land (Deuteronomy 34:1-4)
decisions.reason: Matthew tells of several mountains (5:1; 17:1; 28:16), but does not say so here.

decisions.choice: takes, shows (L); took, showed (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration, as in 4:5.

records.source: τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ὕπαγε, Σατανᾶ· γέγραπται γάρ· Κύριον τὸν θεόν σου προσκυνήσεις καὶ αὐτῷ μόνῳ λατρεύσεις.
records.gloss: Then says to him the Jesus, Go away, Satan; it has been written for: Lord the God of you you will worship and him alone you will serve.
pieces: "Get away, Satan!" Jesus said to him. "For Scripture says, 'You must worship the Lord your God and serve no one but {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.'"

L.10: Then Jesus says to him, "Go away, Satan, for it is written, 'You shall worship [the] Lord your God and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} only.'"

R.10: Jesus said to him, "Go away, Satan! The Scriptures say, 'Worship the Lord your God. Serve only {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.'"

decisions.choice: Satan: the adversary, the devil's Hebrew name
decisions.reason: Satan means adversary or accuser in Hebrew; devil means slanderer in Greek. Both name the same enemy. Jesus later uses the name for Peter when Peter opposes his way (16:23).

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 6:13: worship and serve God alone
decisions.reason: The verse warns Israel not to follow other gods in the land. Matthew's wording has "worship" where Deuteronomy has "fear", which answers the devil's demand directly.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God, whose name stands in the Hebrew
decisions.reason: In Deuteronomy 6:13 the Hebrew has God's name, which the Greek Old Testament gives as "Lord". The Lord your God is the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: serve: serve in worship
decisions.reason: The verb is used of religious service and worship.

decisions.choice: says (L); said (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: τότε ἀφίησιν αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄγγελοι προσῆλθον καὶ διηκόνουν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: Then leaves him the devil, and behold, angels came and were serving him.
pieces: Then the devil left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and angels came and took care of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.11: Then the devil leaves {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and look, angels came and were serving {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.11: Then the devil left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and angels came to take care of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: were serving him: caring for him, probably with food
decisions.reason: The verb is used of serving at table and of care in general (8:15). After the fast, God provides; Jesus did not have to throw himself down for angels to come (4:6).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this word to point to what comes next. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal uses "look", and Balanced and Readable carry its force in the flow of the sentence, as in 1:20.

records.source: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὅτι Ἰωάννης παρεδόθη ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.
records.gloss: Having heard then that John was handed over he withdrew into the Galilee.
pieces: News reached Jesus that John had been arrested, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went back to Galilee.

L.12: Now when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard that John had been handed over, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} withdrew into Galilee.

R.12: Jesus heard that John had been put in prison. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went back to Galilee.

decisions.choice: handed over: arrested and imprisoned
decisions.reason: Matthew tells of John's arrest by Herod Antipas later (14:3). The same verb is used of Jesus being handed over to death (17:22; 26:2): John's path goes before his.

decisions.choice: withdrew: went away, as Matthew says when danger is near
decisions.reason: Matthew uses the same verb in 2:12-22 and 12:15. Galilee was ruled by the same Herod who arrested John, so Jesus does not go there to be safe; Matthew gives the reason in 4:14.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins here, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

records.heading: Jesus begins in Galilee

records.source: καὶ καταλιπὼν τὴν Ναζαρὰ ἐλθὼν κατῴκησεν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ τὴν παραθαλασσίαν ἐν ὁρίοις Ζαβουλὼν καὶ Νεφθαλίμ·
records.gloss: And having left the Nazareth having come he settled in Capernaum the [one] by the sea in regions of Zebulun and Naphtali;
pieces: He left Nazareth and went to live in Capernaum, a town by the sea in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali.

L.13: And leaving Nazareth, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came and settled in Capernaum, which is by the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali,

R.13: He left Nazareth and moved to Capernaum, a town by Lake Galilee. It was in the land that once belonged to the tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali.

decisions.choice: Capernaum: a fishing town on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Capernaum became Jesus's base in Galilee; Matthew later calls it "his own town" (9:1).

decisions.choice: Zebulun and Naphtali: the old lands of two northern tribes
decisions.reason: These tribal lands lay west of the Sea of Galilee. They were the first part of Israel to fall to Assyria (2 Kings 15:29), which is why Isaiah speaks of their darkness (4:16).

decisions.choice: by Lake Galilee
decisions.reason: The "sea" is the freshwater lake of Galilee. Readable says so.

decisions.choice: the sentence continues into 4:14 with a comma
decisions.reason: The Greek sentence goes on into 4:14 ("so that ..."). Literal ends this record with a comma; Balanced and Readable start a new sentence.

records.source: ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·
records.gloss: that might be fulfilled the [thing] spoken through Isaiah the prophet saying:
pieces: This was so that the word spoken through the prophet Isaiah would be fulfilled:

L.14: so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:

R.14: This made what the prophet Isaiah had said come true:

decisions.choice: so that it might be fulfilled: Jesus's move belongs to God's purpose
alternatives: it happened to match the prophecy
decisions.reason: Matthew's fulfillment sayings (1:22; 2:15, 23) show events taking place as Scripture said. Here Jesus's move to Capernaum fulfills Isaiah 9:1-2.

records.source: Γῆ Ζαβουλὼν καὶ γῆ Νεφθαλίμ, ὁδὸν θαλάσσης, πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, Γαλιλαία τῶν ἐθνῶν, ὁ λαὸς ὁ καθήμενος ἐν σκοτίᾳ φῶς εἶδεν μέγα, καὶ τοῖς καθημένοις ἐν χώρᾳ καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου φῶς ἀνέτειλεν αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, way of sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles, \v 16 the people the sitting in darkness light saw great, and to the [ones] sitting in region and shadow of death light rose to them.
pieces: "Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, along the road by the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee where the Gentiles live:
the people who sat in darkness saw a great light, and for those who sat in the land of death's shadow, light rose like the dawn."

L.15: "Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, [the] way of [the] sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles,
L.16: the people sitting in darkness saw a great light, and for those sitting in [the] region and shadow of death, light dawned on them."

R.15: "The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali are on the road by the sea, on the other side of the Jordan River. It is Galilee, where many people who are not Jews live.
R.16: The people who lived in darkness have seen a great light. They lived in a land where death was close, like a dark shadow. But now a light has come to them, like the sun coming up."

decisions.choice: Isaiah 9:1-2: light for the north, before the promise of a child king
alternatives: a description of the region only
decisions.reason: Isaiah promises that the land humbled first by Assyria will see a great light, and goes on to the child born to reign on David's throne (Isaiah 9:6-7). Matthew sees the light dawn as Jesus begins his work in Galilee.

decisions.choice: Galilee of the Gentiles: a region where many non-Jews lived
decisions.reason: Galilee was surrounded by Gentile lands and had many Gentile residents. The phrase points ahead to the good news for all nations (28:19).

decisions.choice: sitting in darkness, in the shadow of death: living in despair, with death near
decisions.reason: "Sit" is a Hebrew way of saying live or dwell. Darkness and the shadow of death describe a people without hope (Psalm 107:10); the light is God's salvation.

decisions.choice: the way of the sea: the region along the road toward the sea
alternatives: the coast road to the Mediterranean only
the road by the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: In Isaiah the phrase names a route and the land it passes through; which sea is meant is debated.

decisions.choice: light rose like the dawn (B); like the sun coming up (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the sun rising. Balanced and Readable keep the picture.

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable says who the Gentiles are.

records.source: Ἀπὸ τότε ἤρξατο ὁ Ἰησοῦς κηρύσσειν καὶ λέγειν· Μετανοεῖτε, ἤγγικεν γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
records.gloss: From then began the Jesus to preach and to say, Repent, has come near for the kingdom of the heavens.
pieces: From then on Jesus began to proclaim, "Repent, because the kingdom of heaven has come near."

L.17: From then Jesus began to preach and to say, "Repent, for the kingdom of the heavens has come near."

R.17: From that time Jesus began to preach. He said, "Turn away from your sins and come back to God, because the kingdom of heaven is coming near."

decisions.choice: from then Jesus began: the start of a new stage of the story
decisions.reason: Matthew uses the same words in 16:21 to begin a later stage, when Jesus starts to speak of his death.

decisions.choice: the same message as John's (3:2)
decisions.reason: Jesus takes up John's call in the same words. See the notes on 3:2 for "repent" and "the kingdom of heaven".

decisions.choice: the same wording as 3:2 at each level
decisions.reason: The repeated message is given in the same words, so readers can see it is the same.

records.source: Περιπατῶν δὲ παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἶδεν δύο ἀδελφούς, Σίμωνα τὸν λεγόμενον Πέτρον καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, βάλλοντας ἀμφίβληστρον εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, ἦσαν γὰρ ἁλιεῖς·
records.gloss: Walking then beside the sea of the Galilee he saw two brothers, Simon the [one] called Peter and Andrew the brother of him, casting a net into the sea, they were for fishermen;
pieces: As Jesus walked along the shore of the Sea of Galilee, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} noticed two brothers, Simon, also called Peter, and Andrew his brother, throwing a net into the water. They fished for a living.

L.18: And walking beside the Sea of Galilee, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw two brothers, Simon who is called Peter and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.

R.18: One day Jesus was walking by Lake Galilee. He saw two brothers, Simon, who was also called Peter, and his brother Andrew. They were throwing a net into the lake to catch fish, because they were fishermen.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Galilee: a freshwater lake about thirteen miles long
decisions.reason: The Gospels call the lake a sea. Fishing was a main trade of the towns on its shore.

decisions.choice: called Peter: the name Jesus gave Simon, meaning rock
decisions.reason: Matthew tells how Jesus gives Simon this name in 16:18.

decisions.choice: a net: a round casting net thrown by hand from the shore or the shallows
decisions.reason: The word names the circular net weighted at the edge, which a fisherman threw over the water.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new scene.

records.heading: The first disciples

records.source: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Δεῦτε ὀπίσω μου, καὶ ποιήσω ὑμᾶς ἁλιεῖς ἀνθρώπων.
records.gloss: And he says to them, Come after me, and I will make you fishers of men.
pieces: "Come, follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "and I will make you fishers of {{gender:people|men}}."

L.19: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Come after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will make you fishers of {{gender:people|men}}."

R.19: Jesus said to them, "Come, follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will teach you to catch {{gender:people|men}} instead of fish."

decisions.choice: come after me: become my disciples, following me as your teacher
alternatives: walk behind me for a while
decisions.reason: Disciples walked behind their teacher and learned from him. Jesus calls them to share his life and work.

decisions.choice: fishers of people: they will gather people for God's kingdom
decisions.reason: Jesus turns their trade into a picture of their new work. In Jeremiah 16:16 fishers gather people for judgment; here the call is to bring them into the kingdom (13:47).

decisions.choice: men: human beings
decisions.reason: The word means people in general.

decisions.choice: says (L); said (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: οἱ δὲ εὐθέως ἀφέντες τὰ δίκτυα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: They then immediately having left the nets followed him.
pieces: They left their nets at once and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.20: And immediately they left the nets and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.20: Right away they left their nets and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: followed him: went with him as his disciples
alternatives: walked behind him for a time
decisions.reason: "Follow" in Matthew is the word for being a disciple (8:19-22; 19:27-28).

decisions.choice: immediately ... left: a response with no delay or conditions
decisions.reason: Matthew gives no conversation: the call is answered at once, and the nets that were their living are left behind.

records.source: Καὶ προβὰς ἐκεῖθεν εἶδεν ἄλλους δύο ἀδελφούς, Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ μετὰ Ζεβεδαίου τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν καταρτίζοντας τὰ δίκτυα αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐκάλεσεν αὐτούς.
records.gloss: And having gone on from there he saw other two brothers, James the [son] of Zebedee and John the brother of him, in the boat with Zebedee the father of them mending the nets of them, and he called them.
pieces: A little farther on {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, in their boat with Zebedee their father, repairing their nets. He called them.

L.21: And going on from there, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw two other brothers, James the [son] of Zebedee and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called them.

R.21: Jesus walked on and saw two other brothers, James and John. They were in a boat with their father Zebedee, fixing their fishing nets. Jesus called them to come with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: mending: repairing or getting the nets ready
decisions.reason: The verb means to put in order: to mend torn nets and make them ready for use.

decisions.choice: called them: summoned them to be his disciples
decisions.reason: Matthew gives the words of the call only once (4:19); this call is the same.

decisions.choice: called them to come with him
decisions.reason: Readable says what the call was.

records.source: οἱ δὲ εὐθέως ἀφέντες τὸ πλοῖον καὶ τὸν πατέρα αὐτῶν ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: They then immediately having left the boat and the father of them followed him.
pieces: They left the boat and their father without delay and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.22: And immediately they left the boat and their father and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.22: Right away they left the boat and their father and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: left the boat and their father: their work and their family
decisions.reason: Sons worked in the family trade. Leaving father and boat shows the cost of following Jesus, which he speaks of later (10:37; 19:29).

records.source: Καὶ περιῆγεν ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ, διδάσκων ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν καὶ κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ θεραπεύων πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν ἐν τῷ λαῷ.
records.gloss: And he was going about in all the Galilee, teaching in the synagogues of them and proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.
pieces: Jesus went from place to place all over Galilee. He taught in their synagogues, announced the gospel of the kingdom, and healed every disease and every illness among the people.

L.23: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went about in all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.

R.23: Jesus went all over Galilee. He taught in the Jewish meeting places called synagogues. He told people the good news about God's kingdom. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed people of every kind of sickness and disease.

decisions.choice: their synagogues: the meeting places of the Jews of Galilee
decisions.reason: In a synagogue a town's Jews gathered on the Sabbath for prayer and the reading and teaching of Scripture. Visiting teachers could be invited to speak.

decisions.choice: the gospel of the kingdom: the good news that God's rule is coming
decisions.reason: The good news is what Jesus proclaimed in 4:17: the kingdom of heaven has come near.

decisions.choice: teaching, proclaiming, healing: a summary of Jesus's work
decisions.reason: Matthew repeats this summary almost word for word in 9:35. Between the two come Jesus's teaching (chapters 5-7) and his healings (chapters 8-9).

decisions.choice: the Jewish meeting places called synagogues; God's kingdom
decisions.reason: Readable says what a synagogue was and whose kingdom is meant.

records.heading: Teaching and healing in Galilee

records.source: καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ἡ ἀκοὴ αὐτοῦ εἰς ὅλην τὴν Συρίαν· καὶ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας ποικίλαις νόσοις καὶ βασάνοις συνεχομένους, δαιμονιζομένους καὶ σεληνιαζομένους καὶ παραλυτικούς, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτούς.
records.gloss: And went out the report of him into all the Syria; and they brought to him all the badly having, with various diseases and torments being gripped, being demon-possessed and being moonstruck and paralytics, and he healed them.
pieces: News about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} spread through all Syria, and people brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} everyone who was ill: those suffering from all kinds of diseases and pain, people controlled by demons, people who had seizures, and people who could not move. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.

L.24: And the report about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} went out into all Syria, and they brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all who were ill, gripped by various diseases and torments, demon-possessed and epileptics and paralytics, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.

R.24: People all over Syria heard about Jesus. They brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} everyone who was sick. Some had different diseases or terrible pain. Some had demons in them. Some had seizures, and some could not move their bodies. Jesus healed them.

decisions.choice: Syria: the lands to the north and east of Galilee
alternatives: the whole Roman province including Judea
decisions.reason: The news spread beyond the Jewish lands into the wider region to the north.

decisions.choice: epileptics: people who had seizures, thought to be moonstruck
decisions.reason: The word means "moonstruck". People linked seizures with the moon; the symptoms described in 17:15 are those of epilepsy.

decisions.choice: demon-possessed: under the control of evil spirits
decisions.reason: Matthew distinguishes people with demons from those with illnesses, and tells of Jesus driving demons out (8:28-34).

decisions.choice: people who had seizures; people who could not move
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the conditions instead of using medical labels.

records.source: καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ Δεκαπόλεως καὶ Ἱεροσολύμων καὶ Ἰουδαίας καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου.
records.gloss: And followed him crowds many from the Galilee and Decapolis and Jerusalem and Judea and beyond the Jordan.
pieces: Great crowds followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and the region beyond the Jordan.

L.25: And large crowds followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from Galilee and [the] Decapolis and Jerusalem and Judea and beyond the Jordan.

R.25: Large crowds of people followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They came from Galilee and from the Ten Towns. They came from Jerusalem and Judea and from the land on the other side of the Jordan River.

decisions.choice: the Decapolis: a league of ten Greek cities, mostly east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The name means "ten cities". Their people were largely Gentile.

decisions.choice: crowds followed him: they went after him, though they were not yet disciples
decisions.reason: Matthew keeps the crowds distinct from the disciples he has just called. Both hear the teaching that follows (5:1; 7:28).

decisions.choice: the Ten Towns
decisions.reason: Readable translates the name.
